7.english: «Addition» this is who the action falls on

7.arabic: الفَاعِلُ:  اسْمٌ مَرْفُعٌ قَبْلَهُ فِعْلٌ: وَ هُوَ الَّذِي فَعَلَ الفِعْلَ
7.english: «Actor» - it is the subject that always appears in the nominative after the verb
«The man heard the adhan» (the man in the example is the actor in the nominative case)

7.arabic: الْمَفْعُولُ بِهِ:      اسْمٌ مَنصُوبٌ وَقَعَ عَلَيْهِ فِعْلُ الفَاعِلِ
7.english: «Addition» — it is the one on whom the action falls. Which is always in the accusative case, comes after the character
«The kids hit the dog» (dog in example «addition»)
1 option - when he stands as a separate word
2 option -  when it is fused with the possessive pronoun
In Arabic, a proposal cannot contain two actors. A verb with a character cannot be at the beginning of a sentence. It must be singular without a fused pronoun ед. ч.
When in a sentence the first verb follows the protagonist of the denoting persons, then the second verb in the sentence agrees with it in gender and number
3 option - this is when the verb «character» and «addition» come together in one word

9.english: Additional clauses in Arabic can join the main clause using a subordinate conjunction (   أَنّ ) «What», immediately followed by the subject accusative
«what» - it is a conjunction that puts after itself the subject in the nominative case, and the predicate in the accusative case

9.arabic: أَنَّ: ﻻَ تُنْطَقُ، وَلَا تُكتَبُ، فِي أَوَّلِ الْكَلَامِ
9.english: Union «what» - not pronounced or written at the beginning of a word
«I think the teacher has not returned»
